findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission stores resource UUIDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() the code iterates resources of type "Groups" and adds `groupResource.getId()` to the granted set. Resource IDs are UUIDs and are NOT real group IDs. Because V2 builds all-groups authorization on a single schema-typed resource rather than per-group resources, `findByName(server, groupResource.getId())` always returns null and execution falls back to `getResourceTypeResource(...)`. Any scenario where `hasPermission` succeeds (e.g. an admin granted VIEW_MEMBERS on the all-groups resource directly) results in the all-groups resource's UUID being added. Downstream consumers (UsersResource.getUsersCount, BruteForceUsersResource/UsersResource.searchForUser, which set `UserModel.GROUPS` to this set and pass it to `session.users().getUsersCount(..., groupIds)`/`searchForUserStream(..., GROUPS=...)`) treat these strings as group IDs. As a result, for an admin who only has VIEW_MEMBERS on all-groups, user search returns zero users and the count endpoint reports zero even though the admin should see users of all groups. V1's equivalent uses `resource.getName().substring(RESOURCE_NAME_PREFIX.length())`; V2 needs to either return group IDs (resource names) or adopt a sentinel "all groups" semantics understood by callers, plus the search/count code must be consistent with the chosen semantics. This is not covered by the existing tests, which only grant view-members on specific groups.

findings.title: NullPointerException risk in hasPermission when getResourceTypeResource returns null
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission, after `resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` the code immediately calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()`. However, AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource returns null when `supportsAuthorizationSchema(session, resourceServer)` is false (e.g. the admin permissions client lookup fails or the schema resource has not yet been initialized at very early lifecycle stages). Calling `policyStore.findByResource(server, null)` will pass null into the policy store, which throws NullPointerException. Add a null check on the result of `getResourceTypeResource` before the findByResource call and return false if null. The same pattern exists in UserPermissionsV2.java at line 111.

findings.title: Same null-deref risk as in GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission
findings.body: The UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission method assigns the result of `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` to `resource` and then unconditionally passes it to `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()`. If `getResourceTypeResource` returns null (it can, per AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource when supportsAuthorizationSchema is false), this throws NPE. Add a null check.

findings.title: getResourceName ignores GROUPS resource type
findings.body: getResourceName only contains a branch for `USERS.getType().equals(resourceType)`. With GROUPS now a first-class resource type in SCHEMA, policies for groups fall through to `return resource.getDisplayName();`. For specific group resources the `getName()` is the group's ID (per `resolveGroup`) and the display name is typically unset, so the admin UI and policy listings will show an empty string or the group id rather than the group's actual name. Add a parallel branch similar to the users branch that resolves the GroupModel by `resource.getName()` and returns `group.getName()` (and for the "all-groups" schema resource return a label such as "All groups"). This is a function gap introduced by adding the GROUPS resource type without updating this method.

findings.title: Missing permission.getResourceId() filter, inconsistent with UserPermissionsV2
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission iterates returned permissions checking only the scope names, without verifying `permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId())`. The corresponding UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission does include this check. If `root.evaluatePermission(...)` ever returns a permission whose resource is not the one we are evaluating (e.g. due to policy inheritance or shared scope names across resource types), GroupPermissionsV2 would grant access based on that foreign permission. For parity with UserPermissionsV2 and to avoid potential cross-resource grants, add `if (permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId()))` around the inner scope loop.

findings.title: Double semicolon on field initializer
findings.body: `private final GroupRepresentation topGroup = new GroupRepresentation();;` contains a stray second semicolon. It is legal Java but is a lint-grade mistake worth fixing.

findings.title: registerListener now only registers when FGAP V1 feature is enabled at startup
findings.body: The previous behavior registered a ProviderEventListener unconditionally and gated the handler body with a `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` check at every event. The change moves the check outside so the listener is only registered when the V1 feature is enabled. This is functionally equivalent for static feature flags, but it is a behavioral contract change: callers that rely on registering then toggling the feature flag, or that replay events captured before the flag was disabled, will not see the old gating. Either keep registration unconditional (for runtime-toggle safety) or document the new behavior. Not a bug per se but worth a note in commit message / release notes.
